causes.what: Hypervisor hv-01 is CPU-saturated (about 96-98% util, CPU ready about 35%), probably from an unmonitored noisy-neighbour VM or workload. This starves the VMs it hosts (app-01, app-02, cache-01), and the slowness and job-queue backlog cascade up to the web tier.

evidence: hv-01 hv.cpu.util.pct jumped from a steady 40-52% to 95.9% at 19:02:16 and stayed at 95-99%.
hv-01 hv.cpu.ready.pct jumped from about 1-3% to 37.7% at 19:02:02 and stayed at 30-38%.
The first alerts (app-02 at 19:02:59, cache-01 at 19:03:29, app-01 at 19:03:39) are all on VMs hosted on hv-01 and fired within about 1 minute of the hv-01 step change.
The app VMs themselves are not CPU-bound (app-01 cpu 26%, app-02 not checked), so the pressure is on the host, not inside the guests.

app-01 app.queue.depth is 650 and app.resp.ms is 2655, versus app-03 (not on hv-01) at queue 55 and resp 763. Web resp is 2.1-2.5 s on web-01 and web-03 with low CPU. The web alerts follow from the slow app and cache tier.
db-01 (db.io.wait 5%, repl lag 2.4s, conn 67), nas-01 (latency 3.8 ms) and network ping/loss are all normal, which rules out the database, storage and network.
hv-02 and the web VMs on it were not the origin, since their CPU is low (web-03 cpu 30%).
